entries.sentence: Osteoporosis often causes no symptoms, so many people do not know they have it.
entries.note: Versus Arthritis: often has no symptoms.

entries.sentence: The first sign is often a broken bone after a minor fall or accident.
entries.note: First sign is a break from a relatively minor fall or accident.

entries.sentence: Fractures are most likely in the hip, spine or wrist.
Because the bones are more prone to break, a fracture can also happen during routine activities.
entries.note: MedlinePlus: loss of minerals makes bones more prone to fracture, even during routine activities (from search summary).

entries.sentence: Bones of the spine, called vertebrae, can weaken and lose height, which can cause back problems.
entries.note: Versus Arthritis: back problems if vertebrae weaken and lose height.

entries.sentence: If several vertebrae are affected, the spine can start to curve and a person may become shorter.
Sometimes these crush fractures of the spine make breathing difficult.
entries.note: Vertebral crush fractures can make breathing difficult.

entries.sentence: After a fracture, care often starts in accident and emergency (A&E), and pain relief can include painkillers such as paracetamol or codeine.
entries.note: Search summary of Versus Arthritis: treatment typically starts in A&E; painkillers such as paracetamol, codeine, occasionally morphine, NSAIDs.

entries.sentence: The NHS Wales encyclopaedia says osteoporosis is normally assessed and managed by a GP, who may request a bone density scan.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales summary: assessed and managed by GP who may request a DXA scan.

entries.sentence: A DXA scan is a low-dose X-ray test that is quick, painless and does not involve any cuts or needles.
entries.note: Search summary: low-dose X-ray, quick, painless, noninvasive (NIAMS wording 'noninvasive'); NHS page title is the scan 'how it is performed'. Needles not stated; 'no cuts or needles' is a paraphrase of non-invasive.

entries.sentence: The person lies on a padded table while a scanner arm passes over the body, and then goes home afterwards.
entries.note: Search summary: lie on padded table, scanner arm passes over, can go home afterward. Summary blended several leaflets; NHS page attribution not confirmed.

entries.sentence: Clinics usually ask people not to take calcium supplements for a set time beforehand, and otherwise normal medicines and meals continue.
entries.note: Search summary of UK leaflets; exact page not identified.

entries.sentence: The scan does not predict fractures perfectly: someone with low bone density may never break a bone, while someone with average bone density may have several fractures.
entries.note: NIAMS bone mineral density page, as summarised.

entries.sentence: Clinicians also weigh lifestyle factors such as diet, exercise, alcohol use and smoking history when they assess bone health.
entries.note: Search summary: clinicians weigh lifestyle factors alongside bone density study.

entries.sentence: NIAMS describes proper nutrition, exercise and fall prevention as the main parts of treatment, with medicines added where needed.
entries.note: Search summary of NIAMS: nutrition, exercise, fall prevention; medications can be added.

entries.sentence: Medicines are chosen by a clinician from individual factors, and are usually considered when fracture risk is high.
entries.note: Search summary: medicines chosen by clinician based on individual factors; used when diagnosed by bone density study and fracture risk is high.

entries.sentence: NHS Wales says the most common drug treatment is a bisphosphonate, taken alongside calcium and vitamin D.
Versus Arthritis says bisphosphonates can be used to lower the risk of hip and spine fractures.
entries.note: Versus Arthritis bisphosphonates page, as summarised.

entries.sentence: Other options it lists include teriparatide, raloxifene, calcitonin, denosumab and hormone replacement therapy.
Teriparatide is usually used only in severe cases, such as people with several fractures, very low bone density, or when other treatments have not worked.
entries.note: Versus Arthritis teriparatide page, as summarised.

entries.sentence: Oral bisphosphonates commonly cause upper gut problems such as acid reflux, irritation of the food pipe and ulcers.
entries.note: Search summary of reviews on bisphosphonate side effects; exact page for this sentence not confirmed.

entries.sentence: A rare jaw bone problem has been reported, and in most osteoporosis cases dental surgery or jaw injury came first.
entries.note: Review: in most osteoporosis cases dental surgery and/or trauma to jaw were preceding factors.

entries.sentence: Unusual thigh bone fractures are very uncommon but linked with how long the treatment has lasted, so reviews suggest regular check-ups for people on these medicines.
entries.note: Review: AFF very uncommon, associated with duration; regular review advised.

entries.sentence: Versus Arthritis says weight-bearing activities such as walking help bone, while balance and muscle work can lower the chance of falling.
entries.note: Weight-bearing, balance and muscle work (search summary).

entries.sentence: It adds that T'ai Chi can be very effective in reducing the risk of falls.
NIAMS advises people with osteoporosis to avoid high-impact exercise, and to talk to a doctor or physical therapist before starting an exercise programme.
Versus Arthritis likewise says not every high-impact activity is suitable once osteoporosis is present.
entries.note: These exercises might not all be suitable if you have osteoporosis.

entries.sentence: The main dietary advice is a healthy diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, with supplements used when the diet does not supply enough.
entries.note: Search summary: diet rich in calcium and vitamin D; supplements only if diet lacks.

entries.sentence: Taking steps to prevent falls inside and outside the home can help prevent fractures.
MedlinePlus gives examples such as removing hazards like throw rugs, avoiding heelless slippers, and being aware of medicines that cause drowsiness or unsteadiness.
entries.note: Search summary: throw rugs, heelless slippers, drowsy medicines.

entries.sentence: NHS Wales says women are affected more often because oestrogen levels fall after the menopause, which can lead to a rapid drop in bone density.
Versus Arthritis explains that steroids taken by mouth can reduce the calcium absorbed from the gut and increase calcium lost through the kidneys.
Versus Arthritis lists long-term steroid use, early menopause, too little weight-bearing exercise, poor diet, smoking, heavy drinking and family history among the risks for the condition.
It also says drinking a lot of alcohol reduces the body's ability to make bone.
A research review describes a spine fracture as a hallmark of osteoporosis that is linked with a higher chance of further fractures.
entries.note: Search summary: vertebral fractures hallmark and increased risk of subsequent fractures; page attribution to PMC6679098 not confirmed; figures deliberately omitted.

entries.sentence: Osteoporosis often has no symptoms, and the first sign is often a broken bone after a minor fall or accident.
Some people notice back problems if spine bones weaken and lose height, and several affected vertebrae can make the spine curve.
A GP appointment is the usual route for concerns about bone health.
entries.note: NHS Wales: osteoporosis normally assessed and managed by GP; simplified.

entries.sentence: A DXA scan is described as a quick, painless, non-invasive test using a low dose of X-ray.
The person lies on a padded table while a scanner arm passes over.
Radiation exposure is described as small, and people go home afterwards.
entries.note: Search summary of UK leaflets; exact page not confirmed.

entries.sentence: NHS Wales says women are more affected because oestrogen levels fall after the menopause.
This fall can lead to a rapid decrease in bone density.
Other risks named include long-term steroid medicines, family history, smoking and heavy drinking, so men can be affected too.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales risk list; 'men can be affected too' is an inference, since the risks listed apply to anyone.

entries.sentence: Weight-bearing activity such as walking, strength work and balance exercises are described as helpful.
NIAMS advises avoiding high-impact exercise, and Versus Arthritis says some high-impact activities may not be suitable.
People are advised to speak to a doctor or physical therapist before starting a programme.
Oral bisphosphonates commonly cause upper gut problems such as reflux and ulcers.
Rare problems include a jaw bone problem and unusual thigh bone fractures, both linked in reviews to longer treatment.
Regular review of treatment is suggested, and the prescriber decides about any change.
A broken bone after a minor fall or accident
Hip, spine and wrist
DXA bone density scan, a quick painless low-dose X-ray
Bisphosphonates, alongside calcium and vitamin D
Weight-bearing, muscle strengthening and balance exercises
The GP, who may request a bone density scan

contradictions: No contradiction with the existing entry. Note: NIAMS advises avoiding high-impact exercise while Versus Arthritis says high-impact exercise helps prevention but may not suit people who already have osteoporosis; the article states both. The existing entry's prevention line (exercise in youth) is consistent.
